Nkrumah argues that disunity leads to dangers such as the world’s disregard for African independence, as shown by the examples of the French atomic tests and the UN’s ineffective response in the Congo.  
He emphasizes that a united Africa would command respect because the world respects “size and influence.”  
Therefore, the reason he urges avoiding disunity is that the world community sees power as a function of size and influence — disunity makes Africa weak in the eyes of the world.
